## What the states mean

| State | What it actually says |
|---|---|
| MERGED | its feature module is on `origin/main`, read out of git |
| READY TO MERGE | committed, nothing uncommitted - waiting on the merge |
| committed, still editing | has a commit AND is still writing |
| WRITING | files changed, nothing committed yet |
| no work yet | worktree exists, nothing written |
| stopped, no output | tab closed with no files written and no commit |

`WRITING` is measured from the worktree's git state, not from the agent's
screen. A screen can look busy while nothing has been written, which is
exactly the state that is hardest to tell from working - so the dashboard
reads what is on disk.

A **tab closed with no output** is the one state worth acting on: that
agent's work does not exist anywhere, and re-dispatching its workflow is
cheaper than waiting.
